title: "Aciclovir (oral) - Tod et al. 2001"

# Pharmacokinetics of Oral Acyclovir in Neonates and in Infants: a Population Analysis (Tod M, Lokiec F, Bidault R, De Bony F, Petitjean O, Aujard Y, and the Acyclovir Pediatric French Group, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2001)

Reference: doi:10.1128/AAC.45.1.150-157.2001 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2001;45(1):150-157; Table 3).

**Model type: parametric population pharmacokinetic model** (nonlinear mixed-effects, FOCE with interaction, NONMEM IV). Suitable for simulation and MAP Bayesian estimation. Caution: apparent oral parameters (CL/F, V/F), and the power residual error model is approximated by a combined error (see Notes).

## Notes

- Study: prospective French multicentre study, 79 immunocompetent children younger than 2 years with proven or suspected HSV or VZV infection treated with an oral acyclovir suspension (400 mg/10 mL) for at least 5 days: 24 mg/kg every 8 h (< 1 month) or 24 mg/kg four times a day (at 0, 4, 8, 12 and 24 h; 1 month to 2 years). 212 plasma samples at steady state (pre-dose, 2, 3, 5 and 8 h, or a single sample at 4 h in outpatients), radioimmunoassay. Median (range) PNA 5.45 (0.10-23.1) months, PCA 15.45 (8.80-33.1) months, weight 6.90 (1.80-13.0) kg, height 65.0 (43.0-95.0) cm, SCR 39.6 (22.0-98.0) umol/L (Table 1). Oral route only.
- Dose: `amt` in mg of aciclovir (oral suspension). The authors worked in micromoles and micromolar; the model is coded in mg and mg/L (molar mass 225.2 g/mol, 1 umol/L = 0.2252 mg/L), which does not change CL/F, V/F or ka.
- Structure: one-compartment model, first-order absorption and elimination (a two-compartment model was not better; zero-order absorption was worse). Apparent parameters: F is not identifiable from the oral data and is set to 1 (theta1 "accounts for the unknown F"). The global analysis combining these data with 18 children treated intravenously estimated F = 0.118 (CV 16%), but the final IV parameters of that analysis are not reported, so no IV model is coded.
- Clearance (Table 3 and text): CL/F (L/h) = theta1 x GFR x (BSA/1.73) x (40/SCR), with GFR (L/h/1.73 m2) = 7.2 x PCA^theta3 / (theta2^theta3 + PCA^theta3) (maximal adult GFR 7.2 L/h/1.73 m2, i.e. 120 mL/min/1.73 m2), theta1 = 25.5, theta2 = 13.4 months (PCA at half-maximal GFR), theta3 = 6.17; SCR in umol/L (40 = median); BSA (m2) = 0.02667 x HT^0.38217 x WT^0.53937 (Gehan and George formula for children < 5 years, as in the article).
- PCA (postconceptional age, months) is computed in the model with the rules of the article: 1 month = 30 days = 4.33 weeks; PCA = GA/4.33 + PNA/30 for PNA <= 3 months, and PCA = PNA/30 + 9 for PNA > 3 months (GA in weeks, PNA in days). PCA, GFR and BSA are captured.
- Volume: V/F (L) = theta4 x (WT/6.9), theta4 = 37.0 L. Absorption: ka = theta5 = 0.277 h-1.
- Default covariates: medians of Table 1: WT 6.9 kg, HT 65 cm, SCR 39.6 umol/L, PNA 164 days (5.45 months). GA 39 weeks is assumed (not reported; it does not enter PCA when PNA > 3 months). The default PCA is 14.5 months (median of the study 15.45 months; medians of PNA and PCA are not additive).
- IIV (Table 3, variances, used directly): CL/F 0.245 (CV 49%), V/F 0.324 (CV 57%). The variance on ka was estimated near zero (2.98 x 10^-8) and is not included.
- Residual error: power model C = Cpred + eps x Cpred^b, with sigma^2 = 0.210 and b = 0.760 in umol/L (CV 61% at 0.3 uM, 35% at 3 uM, 20% at 30 uM). In mg/L the SD is 0.320 x C^0.76. **Ambiguity:** a power error cannot be represented by the proportional/additive sigma pair required by mapbayr. **Choice:** combined error fitted (least squares on the log SD) to the power model over 0.1-15 mg/L: proportional SD 0.247 (variance 0.0610) and additive SD 0.078 mg/L (variance 0.00608). The approximation is close for 0.3-15 mg/L (CV 36% vs 43% at 0.3 mg/L, 26% vs 32% at 1 mg/L, 25% vs 18% at 10 mg/L) and overestimates the error below 0.2 mg/L.
- Targets used by the authors: time above 2.5 uM (0.56 mg/L, worst-case IC50 for HSV) and 5 uM (1.13 mg/L, VZV) > 12 h per 24 h.
- Simulation check: the typical CL/F of the default child is 27.9 L/h (post hoc median 20.9 L/h, Table 4). Daily AUC at steady state (article, Table 6, medians of 500 simulated children): 441 uM.h (99 mg.h/L) at 0-1 month with 24 mg/kg three times a day, 269 uM.h (61 mg.h/L) at 1-3 months, 93 uM.h (21 mg.h/L) at 3-12 months and 76 uM.h (17 mg.h/L) at 12-24 months with 24 mg/kg four times a day. The typical values for representative children of each age range are 94, 65, 23 and 19 mg.h/L, with times above 0.56 / 1.13 mg/L of 24 / 24, 24 / 22.8, 18.2 / 10.2 and 17.2 / 6.2 h (article: 24 / 24, 24 / 22.3, 17.8 / 8.4 and 16.3 / 2.6 h).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(mrgsolve)
library(mapbayr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r model}
code <- '
[PROB]
Tod et al. 2001 - oral aciclovir suspension in neonates and infants < 2 years
(79 children, 212 samples, NONMEM IV FOCE-I). One-compartment model, first-order absorption, apparent parameters (F = 1).
Covariates: CL/F = theta1 x sigmoid GFR maturation with PCA x BSA/1.73 x 40/SCR; V/F proportional to weight.
IIV on CL/F and V/F. Power residual error approximated by a combined error.

[SET] end = 24, delta = 0.1

[PARAM] @annotated
TH1     : 25.5  : Scaling factor of CL/F on estimated GFR (includes 1/F and tubular secretion)
GFRMAX  : 7.2   : Maximal GFR (L/h/1.73 m2)
TH2     : 13.4  : PCA at half-maximal GFR (months)
TH3     : 6.17  : Sigmoidicity coefficient of GFR maturation
SCR_REF : 40    : Reference serum creatinine, median (umol/L)
TVV     : 37.0  : Apparent volume of distribution V/F for 6.9 kg (L)
WT_REF  : 6.9   : Reference weight, median (kg)
TVKA    : 0.277 : Absorption rate constant (1/h)
ETA1    : 0     : IIV CL/F
ETA2    : 0     : IIV V/F

[PARAM] @annotated @covariates
WT  : 6.9  : Body weight (kg)
HT  : 65   : Height (length) (cm)
SCR : 39.6 : Serum creatinine (umol/L)
PNA : 164  : Postnatal age (days)
GA  : 39   : Gestational age (weeks) (ambiguous, see Notes)

[CMT] @annotated
DEPOT : Depot, oral aciclovir dose (mg) [ADM]
CENT  : Central compartment, aciclovir (mg) [OBS]

[MAIN]
double PCA = (PNA > 90) ? (PNA / 30 + 9) : (GA / 4.33 + PNA / 30);
double GFR = GFRMAX * pow(PCA, TH3) / (pow(TH2, TH3) + pow(PCA, TH3));
double BSA = 0.02667 * pow(HT, 0.38217) * pow(WT, 0.53937);
double CL = TH1 * GFR * (BSA / 1.73) * (SCR_REF / SCR) * exp(ETA1 + ETA(1));
double V  = TVV * (WT / WT_REF) * exp(ETA2 + ETA(2));
double KA = TVKA;

[ODE]
dxdt_DEPOT = -KA * DEPOT;
dxdt_CENT  =  KA * DEPOT - CL / V * CENT;

[OMEGA] @annotated
ECL : 0.245 : IIV CL/F (variance, CV 49%)
EV  : 0.324 : IIV V/F (variance, CV 57%)

[SIGMA] @annotated
PROP : 0.0610  : Proportional error (variance), approximation of the power error (ambiguous, see Notes)
ADD  : 0.00608 : Additive error (variance, SD 0.078 mg/L), approximation of the power error (ambiguous, see Notes)

[TABLE]
double IPRED = CENT / V;
double DV = IPRED * (1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2);
int i = 0;
while (DV < 0 && i < 100) { simeps(); DV = IPRED * (1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2); ++i; }

[CAPTURE] @annotated
DV  : Aciclovir plasma concentration (mg/L)
PCA : Postconceptional age (months)
GFR : Estimated GFR (L/h/1.73 m2)
BSA : Body surface area, Gehan and George (m2)
CL  : Individual apparent clearance CL/F (L/h)
V   : Individual apparent volume of distribution V/F (L)
'
mod <- mcode("ACV_Tod", code)
```

```{r simulation}
# Representative children of the four age ranges of Table 6 (typical parameters, SCR 40 umol/L, steady state):
# 0-1 month (GA 39 weeks, PNA 15 d, 3.5 kg, 51 cm): 24 mg/kg every 8 h;
# 1-3 months (PNA 60 d, 4.8 kg, 57 cm), 3-12 months (PNA 210 d, 7.5 kg, 67 cm), 12-24 months (PNA 540 d, 10.5 kg, 80 cm):
# 24 mg/kg at 0, 4, 8, 12 h and 24 h (four doses per 24 h)
kids <- data.frame(ID = 1:4, WT = c(3.5, 4.8, 7.5, 10.5), HT = c(51, 57, 67, 80), PNA = c(15, 60, 210, 540), GA = 39, SCR = 40)
d1 <- kids %>% filter(ID == 1) %>% mutate(time = 0, amt = 24 * WT, ii = 8, addl = 14)
d2 <- kids %>% filter(ID > 1) %>% slice(rep(1:3, each = 4)) %>% group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate(time = c(0, 4, 8, 12), amt = 24 * WT, ii = 24, addl = 4) %>% ungroup()
data <- bind_rows(d1, d2) %>% mutate(evid = 1, cmt = 1) %>% arrange(ID, time)

out <- mod %>%
  zero_re() %>%
  data_set(data) %>%
  mrgsim(end = 120, delta = 0.05) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(time >= 96) %>%
  mutate(time = time - 96, Age = factor(ID, labels = c("0-1 month, q8h", "1-3 months, 4/day", "3-12 months, 4/day", "12-24 months, 4/day")))

# Article (Table 6, medians): daily AUC 99 / 61 / 21 / 17 mg.h/L; time > 0.56 mg/L 24 / 24 / 17.8 / 16.3 h; time > 1.13 mg/L 24 / 22.3 / 8.4 / 2.6 h
out %>% group_by(Age) %>%
  summarise(PCA = PCA[1], CL = CL[1], V = V[1], Cmax = max(DV), Cmin = min(DV),
            AUC24 = sum(diff(time) * (head(DV, -1) + tail(DV, -1)) / 2),
            T_2.5uM = 0.05 * sum(DV > 0.563), T_5uM = 0.05 * sum(DV > 1.126))

ggplot(out, aes(time, DV, colour = Age)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.563, 1.126), linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Aciclovir concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Tod et al. 2001 - oral aciclovir 24 mg/kg, steady state over 24 h")
```
